title: AI Design Suite — per-project verification-vocabulary glossary
description: Schema for a consuming project's own registry of the verification-related terms it actually uses in its own docs and CI output — its own tier names, its own gate-status words, its own maturity labels if they differ from this suite's proven/unverified/experimental/pointer (CLAUDE.md, catalog.py) or from verification-tier.schema.json's unverified/self-tested/cross-verified/human-reviewed. This suite does not require or assume any of those vocabularies from a consuming project: a project is free to call its CI gate status GATE_GREEN, its component tiers 'Tier A/B/C', or anything else, and this file is the one place that spells out what each of ITS OWN terms means, so a reader (human or agent) does not have to reconstruct the meaning from tribal knowledge or by grepping CI scripts. Conventionally .design-suite/verification-glossary.json, pointed to by profile.json's verificationGlossary.file field. This is deliberately a flat lookup table (JSON), not prose, for the same reason component-maturity and component-capabilities are JSON rather than markdown: the primary reader is as often an agent asking 'what does term X mean here' as it is a human, and a flat {term: definition} shape is exact to query and diff, where a markdown glossary would have to be re-parsed and could silently drift in phrasing without a schema to hold it to a shape. `definition` is the only required field per term for the same reason `status` is required in component-maturity.schema.json: a term that is listed but not actually defined is exactly the ambiguity this file exists to remove.

definition.description: What this term means in this project, in plain language, precise enough that someone (or some agent) who has never seen it used before can act on it correctly. Not a restatement of the term itself.

category.description: Loose grouping for filtering, not a controlled vocabulary the way `tier` fields elsewhere are — a project's own set of verification-concept kinds. Common values: 'gate-status' (a CI pass/fail signal like GATE_GREEN), 'component-tier' (a build/release gate like Tier A), 'maturity-label' (a stability tag like this suite's proven/unverified), 'verification-tier' (a per-claim trust level like cross-verified). Free text so a project is never blocked waiting for this schema to add a category it needs.

appliesTo.description: Where this term is actually used, so a reader can go see it in context rather than take the definition on faith — a file path, a CI job name, a PR template field, a doc section. E.g. 'Verification-Tier: trailer in PR descriptions', 'gates.py summary line', 'docs/CATALOG.md maturity column'.

examples.description: Optional concrete examples of the term appearing in real output or docs — a literal CI log line, a doc snippet. Helps distinguish a term from a near-miss (e.g. a status string that looks similar but means something else).

relatedTerms.description: Other keys in this same file's `terms` map that this one is easily confused with, supersedes, or is ordered against (e.g. a tier scale). Optional; free text keys, not validated against `terms` by this schema because a glossary is allowed to be built incrementally with forward references.

notes.description: Caveats, history, or scope limits the definition alone does not carry — e.g. 'renamed from X in 2026-03, old CI logs before that date still say X'. Optional, same rationale as component-maturity.schema.json's `notes` field.

terms.description: Keyed by the literal term exactly as it appears in this project's own docs or CI/tooling output — e.g. 'GATE_GREEN', 'Tier A', 'self-tested' — so a lookup by the literal string a reader just saw resolves directly, with no normalisation step to get wrong. The key is opaque and project-chosen; this schema imposes no vocabulary of its own, only the shape each entry must have once a project picks its terms.

_readme: CANONICAL. This is the schema for a per-project verification-vocabulary glossary file — see docs/ROADMAP.md master backlog (issue #38, item 25) and issue #76 for why this exists and how it differs from this suite's OWN verification vocabularies, which are already defined elsewhere and are not what this file is for: docs/CATALOG.md's maturity labels (proven/unverified/experimental/pointer), CLAUDE.md's tier table (auto/explicit), and verification-tier.schema.json's per-claim tier (unverified/self-tested/cross-verified/human-reviewed, issue #55). Those three are the suite's own fixed vocabularies and are gated or hand-maintained where they live; this schema instead lets a CONSUMING project register whatever verification vocabulary IT uses (its own tier names, its own gate-status words) so that vocabulary has one documented, machine-readable home instead of living only in tribal knowledge or scattered CI script comments. profile.json's optional verificationGlossary.file field points at the populated instance; nothing in the universal plugin hardcodes a project's own term names.
